gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Warnes draws wiry, stretched letters whose strokes taper away before they touch, with no thick-to-thin shift anywhere. And Noto Sans Khmer goes the other way, with generous openings and small letters that stand almost as tall as capitals.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Noto Sans Khojki keeps its exits wide enough for light to pass through, and every e has a big, clear eye. Warnes is the showier one, bold and widely spaced with strokes of uniform thickness, while the sans body simply stays easy to follow.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Expressive and a bit wild, Warnes lays down strokes like fine rope. Make it small, though, and that spacious tracking loses its drama, while Noto Sans Khudawadi, a friendly sans-serif with rounds left unlatched, would hold up fine.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-kr: Bold, expressive Warnes runs a single monoline stroke from start to finish, spaced out and stretched wide. Yet Noto Sans KR sits beside it with stubby ascenders, a big x-height and curves that stay generously open.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-lao: Warnes looks like spaghetti: same-width strokes that taper off before they meet, stretched across wide tracking. Noto Sans Lao feels modern and grounded next to it, with a tall x-height and mouths that stay open on c, e and a.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Loud, stretched and spaced out, Warnes draws its bowls at the same thickness as its stems. But Noto Sans Lao Looped feels like a professional sans-serif beside it, with words that read as solid blocks and bowls left open on one side.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Noto Sans Lepcha reads approachably, with wide curve openings. Warnes does the wirelike, bold, expressive display work in strokes of one thickness, while the plain sans body brings a lowercase as sturdy as cast iron capitals.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Warnes sets its curves as thick as its straight stems, tapering strokes out before they meet, with stretched, spacious tracking. Noto Sans Limbu sits below with gaping curves and tall-bodied small letters, making a friendly, contemporary partner for all that expressive boldness.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Warnes has a bold, pencil-line consistency, stretched wide with strokes that fade out before touching. It earns its keep big and short.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Warnes has round letters whose rims match the stems. Noto Sans Lydian is the approachable one, a sans-serif with capitals barely taller than lowercase and an opening as wide as a sprung paper clip.
